newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-ROBSON SAYS EMERSON STILL IN BRAZIL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ROBSON SAYS EMERSON STILL IN BRAZIL.

text.p: Middlesbrough manager Bryan Robson said on Thursday that missing midfielder Emerson is still in Brazil, visiting his sick aunt.
The four million pounds ($6.4 million) player failed to arrive back in the city on Thursday after flying to Brazil last week for what the club thought was a holiday.
"As soon as I know something, I will let you know," said Robson as he left the club's Riverside Stadium.
"His auntie was taken ill and he has gone to see her. That's the latest I know. Emerson is definitely in Brazil."
Earlier in the day, Robson declared his intention to help Emerson and his girlfriend Andrea settle in the area.
"There are bound to be some problems at a club with 50 players, but I don't expect players to go against their contract, especially only a few months into it," the Boro boss added.

Chairman Steve Gibson has threatened to impose a hefty fine on the four million pounds ($6.6 million) player and ask FIFA to impose a world-wide ban if Emerson continues to defy the club by refusing to return and honour his four-year contract.
Club officials said earlier they were expecting Emerson to return to Middlesbrough on Wednesday and report for training on Thursday.
The 24-year-old Brazilian was then reported as saying in Brazil he would not be coming back to Middlesbrough and wanted to negotiate his release from the club.
Besides his settling in problems, Barcelona's reported interest in the player could also be a factor.
Barcelona boss Bobby Robson reluctantly sold Emerson to Middlesbrough in the summer while he was in charge of Porto and is believed to be interested in recapturing him.
Bryan Robson has stressed that Emerson must honour his contract. "I want to find out what is the truth and what is not.
"Emerson will not be leaving the club. In fact no-one is leaving unless I decide it is in our best interests. I have the full backing of the chairman over this."
